title: Speculative Decoding and Model Parallelism
summary: Decode is memory-bound, so checking several guessed tokens costs almost the same as generating one. Speculative decoding exploits this with a cheap draft model, and keeps the output distribution exactly the same. When a model is too big for one GPU, tensor and pipeline parallelism split it, trading memory for communication.
objectives: Explain draft-and-verify decoding and why the output distribution is unchanged
Derive and compute the expected tokens per target pass, (1 - alpha^(k+1)) / (1 - alpha), and the resulting speedup including draft cost
Choose a draft length k and recognise when speculation stops helping (large batches, low acceptance)
Explain tensor parallelism and estimate its all-reduce communication per layer
Explain pipeline parallelism, compute the bubble fraction and choose between the two
prerequisites: You should know why decode is memory-bound ([Where the Time Goes](/learn/inference-and-serving/memory-and-compute)) and how sampling produces a next-token distribution ([Next-Token Prediction and Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling)).
